In [[probability theory]], '''Yan's theorem''' is a [[Separation theorem|separation]] and existence result. It is of particular interest in [[financial mathematics]] where one uses it to prove the [[Kreps-Yan theorem]].

The theorem was published by [[Jia-An Yan]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Jia-An|last1=Yan|date=1980|title=Caracterisation d' une Classe d'Ensembles Convexes de <math>L^1</math> ou <math>H^1</math>|volume=14|journal=Séminaire de probabilités de Strasbourg|pages=220–222|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/SPS_1980__14__220_0/}}</ref> It was proven for the [[Lp space|L<sup>1</sup> space]] and later generalized by [[Jean-Pascal Ansel]] to the case <math>1\leq p<+\infty</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Jean-Pascal|last1=Ansel|first2=Christophe|last2=Stricker|title=Quelques remarques sur un théorème de Yan|journal=Séminaire de Probabilités XXIV, Lect. Notes Math.|publisher=Springer|date=1990}}</ref>

== Yan's theorem ==
Notation:
:<math>\overline{\Omega}</math> is the [[Closure (topology)|closure]] of a set <math>\Omega</math>.
:<math>A-B=\{f-g:f\in A,\;g\in B\}</math>.
:<math>I_A</math> is the [[indicator function]] of <math>A</math>.
:<math>q</math> is the [[conjugate index]] of <math>p</math>.

=== Statement ===
Let <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)</math> be a [[probability space]], <math>1\leq p<+\infty</math> and <math>B_+</math> be the space of non-negative and bounded [[random variable]]s. Further let <math>K\subseteq L^p(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)</math> be a [[convex set|convex]] subset and <math>0\in K</math>.

Then the following three conditions are equivalent:
# For all <math>f\in L_+^p(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)</math> with <math>f\neq 0</math> exists a constant <math>c>0</math>, such that <math>cf \not\in \overline{K-B_+}</math>.
# For all <math>A\in \mathcal{F}</math> with <math>P(A)>0</math> exists a constant <math>c>0</math>, such that <math>cI_A \not\in \overline{K-B_+}</math>.
# There exists a random variable <math>Z\in L^q</math>, such that <math>Z>0</math> [[almost surely]] and 
:::<math>\sup\limits_{Y\in K}\mathbb{E}[ZY]<+\infty</math>.
